title: ErrorTaxonomy
description: The published error-code taxonomy (SDD §4.3). Every code every tool can emit, each mapped to exactly one recovery class. Entries are an ARRAY so a duplicate code is representable and the one-code-one-recovery schema test can catch it — an object keyed by code would silently collapse duplicates in JSON.parse. `payload` lists the error-object fields that MUST accompany the code (all are optional properties of the envelope's error object; the taxonomy is what makes them required per code).

codes.description: A path argument canonicalizes outside the workspace root(s) (§7.1). The file is not reachable through any retry or rephrasing — give this path up.
The target is protected by workspace or org configuration. A human can amend the protection (§7.2); the agent cannot.
More than one symbol matches. Refine the query using the returned candidates (§4.2 example).
No symbol matches. A revised query (spelling, kind, path scope) can succeed where the same one will not.

The addressed file does not exist in the workspace. The §7.1 jail admits nonexistent in-root paths by design, so ENOENT surfaces at the tool layer. Revise the path — search mode:files locates files by name. Amended in SDD v1.2 (chunk:taxonomy-file-not-found).
The edit would break syntax; the whole batch rolled back (§7.5). Revise the edit using the parser message and the rejected diff — resubmitting the same batch fails identically.
The file changed since the diff was generated. Re-derive anchors against the fresh content hash and retry the same intent (§7.7).
The search pattern does not compile. Fix the pattern; the same one will never succeed.
The requested token budget cannot fit even one result. Raise the budget or narrow the query.
The command is not in the merged config's [commands] table (§9.6). Recovery is abort with the message pointing the human at their config layer — SDD-pinned.

Attempted text/file munging or shell execution via run (§9.6, §1.1): a shell operator, a shell as the program, or a munging program in a program position. The same call will never succeed — use search/read to inspect and edit to modify. v1.5 amendment, chunk:m3-run-tool.
The script exhausted its fuel allowance (§8.1). Split the work into smaller scripts or reduce its scope.
The script attempted a capability it was not granted. Capability grants are a human decision (§8.2).

The script breached its linear-memory cap and was terminated deterministically (§8.1). Reduce the working set — stream over files instead of accumulating them. Added in chunk:m4-script-sandbox: the host's memory-cap kill is a distinct outcome from fuel exhaustion and from capability denial, and one-code-one-recovery forbids folding it into either.
The mode strictly requires a warm index and it is not warm yet (§7.3). Constitution I pins recovery retry; notes carry task progress.

The mutation needs the dry-run→confirm flow (§9.4). The payload carries the HMAC-sealed confirm grant for the offered diff; re-invoke the same call with confirm set to that token (or accept the MRTR elicitation) to apply.
The confirmation token did not match the offered diff (§7.7). Re-run the dry-run→confirm flow against fresh content.
Client/server or on-disk format mismatch. Recovery abort — SDD-pinned (§4.3).
The engine child is down or restarting (§6.2). Recovery retry — SDD-pinned; the supervisor is already restarting it.
A bounded queue is full (§7.7). Recovery retry with the suggested backoff in the payload — SDD-pinned.

The input file repeatedly crashed the engine child and is quarantined from parsing (§6.2); the supervisor refuses it locally until the file changes. Retry cannot help. A human inspects the quarantine record (.workbench/quarantine.jsonl, surfaced by doctor) and fixes or removes the file. Amended in SDD v1.3 (chunk:backlog-quarantine-surfacing).
A plugin exceeded its granted capabilities (§8.4). Widening a grant is a human install-time decision.
The plugin trapped or exhausted fuel and is circuit-breakered unhealthy (§8.1). Stop calling it; core tools continue at full fidelity.
Org policy forbids the requested action (§7.2). Recovery abort — SDD-pinned; the message names the policy layer.
